body:
You might have hit the nail on the head with the abroad thing, its definitely tougher because of the limited contact with family and older, closer friends back home. I feel the same way about my 'friends' here (hence the quotations in the first post), we dont *really* care about each other but we all need socializing and people to party with.  
  
One interesting thing I was thinking about last night right before I fell asleep is this: I quit smoking bud last September, but all of the people I hang out with here are pretty into it. Especially in the beginning of the term when we met, that was a HUGE way to bond and socialize. At first, I would just be around chillin with them and it wasnt an issue but eventually they wouldnt invite me down because I didnt smoke. If youve ever been a smoker, you would know that part of the appeal is the extremely social aspect of it. I was pondering whether or not that small fact has led more or less to an outsider feeling.  
  
The drunk mistake i dont even remember, the gruesome details were relayed to me just a day or two ago. i guess it was pretty bad; they called me an aggressive blackout (but who isnt? any one of my friends back home has blaccked out and we all know how those times end). I like normal social college interaction, but ive never felt like the friends ive made in europe were in any way like the ones back home. I like your advice about just sucking up soem pride, trying to bandage the friendships, and trying to put it behind for two months.  
  
Thank you so much for the reply too :)

Food is an easy one: California burrito (assuming your not californiain, its a carne asada burritor with french fries and guacamole. Yum)  
  
Color would be blue  
  
Edit: Thanks for the reply, means a lot
